2100 — the same margin the three pre-existing error assertions already use, rounded the same
These are bad numbers for a portfolio site to gate on — 0.25 is a failing Lighthouse score by
any normal reading. They are still the honest ones: 'Severities are set to what the site
MEASURES, not to what would be nice' is the rule this whole file opens with, and a threshold
loose enough to look respectable would also be loose enough to never catch a real regression
-- the exact 'green build that proves nothing' failure mode this gate exists to avoid. Tighten
these DOWN as the rendering/hydration work in flight (prerendering, deferred hydration) lands
and lowers the worst-measured number; don't raise them to make a future regression pass.
/playground (the WebGL driving room) is excluded via matchingUrlPattern, not folded into the
worst-case above: its continuous three.js render loop measured 165,393ms of blocking time on
the runner (not a typo — the next-worst URL is 1745ms, two orders of magnitude less). Under
Lighthouse's CPU-throttled trace a real per-frame render loop reads as one enormous blocking
task rather than the many short ones a user actually experiences; that is a known limitation
of lab TBT on canvas-heavy pages, not a regression in this codebase, and a single outlier
would otherwise force every OTHER URL's threshold out past 198,000ms -- the exact loose-gate
failure mode described above, for the other 28 URLs' benefit instead of just this one's.
/playground keeps performance/LCP/FCP/TBT at warn (the global block below still applies to
it) until it has a metric that reflects what it actually is.
